For "Lucky 7 Multiplier" or any game, being late in a run is not automatically good or bad. The same numbers mean different things near the end of a run.

The numbers for "Lucky 7 Multiplier" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
2771.headline: Another top prize was claimed

2772.body:
"Electric 10s" has four of six top prizes left and is about halfway through its run. About a quarter of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, the top prizes and the tickets are going at about the same pace.

The numbers for "Electric 10s" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
2772.headline: How much has sold

2773.body:
"Sugar Skull Cash" is about halfway through its run, with about half of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, a smaller share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a reason to be careful.

The numbers for "Sugar Skull Cash" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
2773.headline: Tickets sold so far

2774.body:
Of the unclaimed prize money on "The Price is Right™", nearly all is in wins under $1,000. The game is a game built around small prizes that are won often. That is neither good nor bad, only how it was designed. Choose the kind of game that fits the win you want.

The numbers for "The Price is Right™" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
2774.headline: How this game pays out

2775.body:
"Casino 7s" is down to three top prizes after a $100,000 winner was claimed in the latest numbers. The game started with four top prizes. Know that before you buy, because a change in top prizes changes the whole game.

Everything here about "Casino 7s" comes from official Texas lottery numbers, current through November 19.
2775.headline: Someone claimed a $100,000 prize

2776.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "Patriotic Payout", about three-quarters are still unsold. The game is near the start of its run, with eight of eight top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Today's free summary of "Patriotic Payout" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.

Of all the tickets printed for "Gnome for the Holidays", most are still unsold. The game is early in its run, with 43 of 57 top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

Every line of Gnome for the Holidays's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
2779.headline: How far along this game is

2780.body:
"Holiday Countdown" has 623,111 prizes of $5 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $1,000 prize, with 48 left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Today's free summary of "Holiday Countdown" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
2780.headline: A close look at the prizes

2781.body:
The most common win left on "The Perfect Gift" is $10. The second biggest prize left is $5,000, and 27 of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Everything above about "The Perfect Gift" comes from the Texas Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
2781.headline: The prize table, line by line

2782.body:
The prize money on "$1,000,000 Diamond Deluxe" leans toward many smaller prizes. It is spread over eight prize levels, from wins equal to the ticket price up to $1 million. Games built like this pay small prizes often and large prizes rarely. That design never changes, and it is the part you choose.

The numbers for "$1,000,000 Diamond Deluxe" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
2782.headline: How the prize money is divided

2783.body:
"30X The Cash" has joined the Texas lineup at $2 with five top prizes of $30,000. Only on the first day do the overall odds describe the game exactly, because nothing has been won. Starting tomorrow, this page shows how that changes.

Everything here about "30X The Cash" comes from official Texas lottery numbers, current through November 19.
2783.headline: New game, all prizes left

2784.body:
"Lucky Scratch" is new from the Texas Lottery. It is a $5 game with four top prizes of $100,000. Nothing big has been won yet because almost no one has played it. This page will show it when that changes.

Every line of Lucky Scratch's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
